bib.title: GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Tables 13-14 (per-task one/few-shot, all sizes) only skimmed, Table 11 and 12 read

question: Can a sparsely activated decoder-only mixture-of-experts LM match or beat dense GPT-3 on zero/one/few-shot tasks at lower training and inference cost?
hypothesis: Sparse MoE decoder-only models can outperform dense models of similar active FLOPs in few-shot in-context learning while saving energy.
contributions: GLaM family of sparse decoder-only MoE LMs up to 1.2T parameters (96.6B active)
Better average than GPT-3 on 29 tasks with about half the inference FLOPs and a third of the training energy
Study of data quality, expert count scaling and data/compute efficiency

method.summary: Decoder-only Transformer with every other feed-forward layer replaced by a 64-expert MoE layer with top-2 gating, trained on a 1.6T-token mixture, plus dense control models trained on the same data. Evaluated zero/one/few-shot on the 29 non-synthetic, non-translation GPT-3 tasks.
method.task: next-token pretraining; in-context evaluation on 29 NLP tasks

datasets.name: GLaM pretraining mixture
datasets.size: 1.6 trillion tokens (Table 3: filtered webpages 143B, Wikipedia 3B, conversations 174B, forums 247B, books 390B, news 650B)
datasets.split: mixture weights 0.42 filtered webpages, 0.06 Wikipedia, 0.28 conversations, 0.02 forums, 0.20 books, 0.02 news
datasets.source: Webpages filtered by a feature-hash linear quality classifier (Pareto sampling by score); public-domain social media conversations from Adiwardana et al. 2020; books, Wikipedia, forums, news
datasets.preprocessing: quality classifier trained to separate curated text (Wikipedia, books, selected websites) from other pages; weights set from small-model performance and to avoid oversampling small sources

datasets.name: 29 evaluation benchmarks
datasets.size: 8 NLG and 21 NLU tasks in 7 categories (App A)
datasets.split: mostly development sets; zero-shot evaluates dev directly; one/few-shot demonstrations drawn randomly from task training set
datasets.source: same suite as Brown et al. 2020 minus 7 synthetic tasks and 6 MT sets

datasets.name: WinoGender, RealToxicityPrompts
datasets.source: Rudinger et al. 2018; Gehman et al. 2020

models.name: GLaM 64B/64E
models.architecture: decoder-only MoE Transformer, 64 experts per MoE layer every other layer, top-2 gating

models.name: GLaM 1.7B/32E,64E,128E,256E
models.layers: 24 base (Table 4 lists 32, 64, 128, 256 in the E column)

other.note: numbers taken from Brown et al. 2020; Gopher 280B and Megatron-NLG 530B given for reference in Table 11

training.objective: cross-entropy language modelling plus MoE auxiliary load-balancing loss from GShard, coefficient 0.01
training.optimizer: Adafactor, beta1=0, beta2=0.99 with 1 - t^-0.8 decay schedule, update clipping 1.0, factored second moments
training.lr_schedule: constant 0.01 for first 10K steps, then inverse square root decay (lr ~ 1/sqrt(t))
training.batch_size: up to 1 million tokens per batch (packed examples)
training.tokens: largest model: results at 280B and 600B tokens (full run 600B per Sec 6.4; dataset 1.6T)
training.regularisation: MoE auxiliary balancing loss; skip updates on NaN/Inf gradients; restart from earlier healthy checkpoint on instabilities
training.hardware: 1,024 Cloud TPU-v4 chips for the 64B/64E model
training.compute: 456 MWh for 600B tokens; 213 MWh for 280B tokens; PUE 1.11; 326W per TPU-v4 chip

other.same_hparams: same learning hyperparameters for all GLaM models
other.sharding: 2D sharding via GSPMD (Xu et al. 2021); experts with same index across layers on same device
other.architecture_mods: per-layer relative positional bias from Transformer-XL; Gated Linear Unit with GELU in non-MoE feed-forward layers

inference.decoding: NLG tasks: beam search width 4; NLU: argmax of option log-likelihood normalized by option token length (non-normalized on ReCoRD and COPA); bias co-occurrence and toxicity: top-k sampling k=40
inference.samples: co-occurrence: 800 outputs per prompt; toxicity: 25 continuations for each of 10K prompts; benchmark runs not stated as repeated
inference.prompting: zero-shot: evaluate dev example directly; one/few-shot: random examples from task train set concatenated with two newlines between demonstration and eval example

parameters.few_shot_k: task-dependent, Table 11 gives shots per task (e.g. 64 for TriviaQA, 1 for one-shot)

metrics.name: accuracy / exact match / F1
metrics.definition: EM and F1 for generative tasks, accuracy for multiple choice, F1a for MultiRC; scores normalized to 0-100

metrics.name: average score
metrics.definition: mean of per-dataset scores over NLG (8) or NLU (21) tasks, or all 29

metrics.name: training energy
metrics.definition: measured system power x chips x time x PUE

baselines: GLaM dense 0.1B, 1.7B, 8B, 137B trained on the same data
eval.protocol: Single reported value per setting; no seeds, no confidence intervals; contamination analysis in App D
